name: Chemify Ltd
subcategory: chemputation: programmable robotic chemical synthesis + AI ('hyperscaler for chemistry')
origin_detail: University of Glasgow spin-out founded by Lee Cronin, Regius Professor of Chemistry at Glasgow, to commercialize his lab's Chemputer, the XDL chemical programming language and the ChemPU literature database. Locations: Glasgow and San Francisco.
flagship_projects: XDL (chemical description language, from the Cronin lab)
openness_notes: The company's Genesis engine, Chemifarm and Curie reactors are proprietary; customers buy 'threads of chempute'. The academic precursor work is public: the Cronin group's GitHub (croningp) hosts ChemputerSoftware (code accompanying the Chemputer Science paper, ~111 stars) and ChemputerAntiviralXDL, but no licence is shown on the org page. Chemify itself has made no open-source releases on its site. Scored 0 for the company; the open academic lineage is noted.

license_history.note: Academic Chemputer/XDL code on GitHub predates it; licence not shown

risk_events: 20 Jun 2025: opened what it calls the world's first chemputation facility (the Chemifarm)
21 Oct 2025: oversubscribed Series B of more than $50M
12 Feb 2026: strategic investment from Zeon Corporation (amount undisclosed)
16 Sep 2026: GBP 22M in grants from Scottish Enterprise and the UK Government
robustness: Supported by equity investors, a Japanese chemicals strategic investor (Zeon) and substantial UK public grants, with pharma collaborations (Dewpoint, Sanacor) and TB/malaria discovery grants. It depends on a founder-scientist's paradigm and a single proprietary facility; the academic code base offers partial continuity.
physical_science_relevance: Very high. Chemify does programmable synthesis of molecules and materials at a dedicated robotic facility. It began as academic digital chemistry (Chemputer, XDL) and now applies it to drug leads and materials with chemical-industry partners such as Zeon.
openness_effect_assessment: Chemify is an academic open-science lineage commercialized as a closed platform. The Cronin lab published Chemputer software and XDL procedures alongside papers, which built the scientific case and community recognition. The company sells proprietary capacity, partly funded by public money (GBP 22M in grants). Fetched sources do not show whether the academic openness helped the company commercially.
key_takeaway: Chemify is the academic-spinout version of the AI-plus-automation chemistry company: a decade of Glasgow research on programmable chemistry (Chemputer, XDL, partly public on GitHub) has become a proprietary 'hyperscaler for chemistry'. By late 2026 it had at least $93M in equity plus GBP 22M of UK public grants, and a Chemifarm facility opened in 2025. Public and academic investment created the paradigm; the commercial asset is closed.
notes: No WebSearch queries were run for this organization (shared WebSearch budget exhausted); facts come from chemify.io, Wikipedia (Leroy Cronin) and GitHub pages listed in fetched_urls.

Licences of the croningp ChemputerSoftware/XDL repositories not shown on the GitHub org page.

contradicted.evidence: CHEMIFY LIMITED ... Incorporated on 24 October 2019 ... Registered office address: School Of Chemistry, University Of Glasgow, Glasgow, Scotland, G12 8QQ
contradicted.note: UK Companies House is the authoritative registry. Its filing history (page 3) shows the company trading before 2022: micro-company accounts to 31 Dec 2020 and 31 Dec 2021, share allotments on 23 Jul and 19 Oct 2021, and a director appointed 23 Jul 2021. Wikipedia (Leroy Cronin) independently says 'launched in 2019'. Chemify's own pages say 2022 ('2022 CHEMIFY FOUNDED' timeline on chemify.io; 20 Jun 2025 release: 'A 2022 spin-out from the University of Glasgow'), which probably marks the formal spin-out or seed round (allotments Feb-Mar 2022). Revert to 2022 if the analysis wants the self-described spin-out year rather than incorporation.

unconfirmed.reason: Only the Series A component has a second page: Wikipedia (Leroy Cronin) says Chemify 'raised £33m in 2023' (about $43M). No independent page found for the >$50M Series B. The company's Business Wire release returned 403, and the 20 Jun 2025 release (reportablenews) gives no funding total. The $93M remains the cited news-page sum (lower bound).

No independent page addresses Chemify's licensing. github.com/chemify holds only a 'github-slideshow' training repo, with no description or website linking it to the company, so it neither confirms nor contradicts openness 0.
